title: Integrative genetics and multiomics analysis reveal mechanisms and therapeutic targets in vitiligo highlighting JAK STAT pathway regulation of CTSS.
authors: Dong, Zi-Yue; He, Ming-Jie; Yu, Yong-Kai; Wang, Fang; Zhao, Peng-Yuan; Ran, De-Long; Fu, De-Shuang; He, Qing; Yang, Run-Ping; Zhang, Jiang-An
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学整合分析研究白癜风遗传机制，涉及JAK/STAT通路调控CTSS，但核心是疾病机制与药物靶点，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅含分子对接但非TF-DNA体系。
abstract: Vitiligo is a complex autoimmune disease characterized by the loss of melanocytes, leading to skin depigmentation. Despite advances in understanding its genetic and molecular basis, the precise mechanisms driving vitiligo remain elusive. Integrating multiple layers of omics data can provide a comprehensive view of disease pathogenesis and identify potential therapeutic targets. The study aims to delineate the genetic and molecular mechanisms of vitiligo pathogenesis using an integrative multiomics strategy. We focus on exploring the regulatory influence of the JAK/STAT pathway on Cathepsin S, a potential therapeutic target in vitiligo. Our GWAS-meta analysis pinpointed five druggable genes: ERBB3, RHOH, CDK10, MC1R, and NDUFAF3, and underwent drug target exploration and molecular docking. SMR analysis linked CTSS, CTSH, STX8, KIR2DL3, and GRHPR to vitiligo through pQTL and eQTL associations. Microarray and single-cell RNA-seq data showed differential expression of CTSS and STAT1/3 in vitiligo patients' blood and skin lesions. Our study offers novel perspectives on vitiligo's genetic and molecular basis, highlighting the JAK/STAT pathway's role in regulating CTSS for antigen processing in melanocytes. Further research is needed to confirm these results and assess the therapeutic potential of CTSS and related genes.
abstract_zh: 白癜风是一种复杂的自身免疫性疾病，其特征是黑色素细胞丧失，导致皮肤脱色素。尽管在理解其遗传和分子基础方面取得了进展，但驱动白癜风的确切机制仍不明确。整合多层次组学数据可以提供疾病发病机制的全景视图，并识别潜在的治疗靶点。本研究旨在利用整合性多组学策略，描绘白癜风发病机制的遗传和分子机制。我们重点探索JAK/STAT通路对组织蛋白酶S（Cathepsin S）的调控影响，后者是白癜风中的一个潜在治疗靶点。我们的GWAS-meta分析确定了五个可成药基因：ERBB3、RHOH、CDK10、MC1R和NDUFAF3，并进行了药物靶点探索和分子对接。SMR分析通过pQTL和eQTL关联将CTSS、CTSH、STX8、KIR2DL3和GRHPR与白癜风联系起来。微阵列和单细胞RNA-seq数据显示，白癜风患者血液和皮肤病变中CTSS和STAT1/3的表达存在差异。我们的研究为白癜风的遗传和分子基础提供了新视角，强调了JAK/STAT通路在调控黑色素细胞中CTSS抗原加工中的作用。需要进一步研究以确认这些结果，并评估CTSS及相关基因的治疗潜力。
